messages:
ashley: FYI I bisected a tail-latency bump on Qwen-14B AWQ int8 after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. 95p latency +18% on long-context workloads. Dumped traces and KV metrics.

devon: ugh. any quick numbers on KV hit rate / microbatch sizes? could be a batching heuristic interacting with kv warmup.

ashley: baseline (pre-change) 95p=120ms, post-change 142ms. KV hit rate drops from ~94% -> ~83% on long sequences (>2k). microbatch stayed at 4. trace id: trace-1756004321-23.

sara: dropping KV hit rate that much smells like a different kernel path evicting or not using prefix cache.

sam: did the selector fallback to the 'fast-rope' kernel? I remember that kernel doesn't support our head-kv-prefetch heuristic and ends up re-computing KV for certain rotatory offsets.

ashley: yes, selector chose kernel:v2-rope-optimized for some shards. I captured kernel decision table: 

```
model: qwen-14b-awq-int8
seq: 2048
heads: 64
kv_dim: 128
kernel_choice: v2-rope-optimized (fallback threshold met for head_stride)
```

sam: that v2 kernel assumes RoPE base scaling aligned to 1.0 canonical rotary. Qwen uses a slightly different rotary frequency due to head_dim packing -> misalignment can cause per-head shifts and cache misses.

marco: remind me — how do we detect that at runtime? do we annotate model metadata with rope_freq/head_stride?

sara: we do, but the selector only checks "rope_scale_approx" boolean. That was relaxed in the change to prefer lower-latency kernels even when rope scale is ~off-by-1. It started picking v2 for a few configurations where it shouldn't.

perf-bot: automated-profile summary for trace-1756004321-23:\n- total_tokens: 4500\n- avg_latency_token_ms: 6.2\n- 95p_token_latency_ms: 18.4\n- kv_cache_hits: 83%\n- kernel_switch_count: 3\n- fallback_rate: 12%\n

devon: ok. Two hypotheses: (A) kernel misselection causing extra KV re-materialization per-layer, (B) int8 AWQ kernel doing extra dequant/qk transforms because it expects contiguous heads.

ashley: I ran a quick microprofile isolating layer 8-12: when v2-rope-optimized is used, per-layer token latency increases by ~40us and a hot loop shows memcpy + small transpose ops every step.

sam: that memcpy/transposes smell like head-layout mismatch. int8 kernels often rely on packed layout (HxK) and if HW path expects different stride we pay copies.

marco: did we try forcing kernel:v1-generic on the same trace to validate? could be a regression introduced in v2.

ashley: forced v1 run: 95p drops back to 118ms, kv hit back to 95%. So v2 is the culprit.

sara: interesting that v1 is faster overall even if slower in hot-path compute — likely because it integrates with our prefix-KV hotset and avoids re-computation. v2 maybe optimizes raw matmul but bypasses hotset advisory hooks.

devon: action items: 1) revert relaxed selector change (temp) 2) add stricter rope_scale/head_stride checks 3) add a micro-benchmark for int8 head-layout cases. I'll own 1 & 2.

sam: I'll add a unit test to the kernel harness that runs packed/unpacked head layouts and measures memcpy overhead. will throw in Mixtral/LLama configs too (different head dims).

marco: also we should record calibration prompt set used for AWQ runs. Ashley — can you paste the calibration prompt snippet you used? we need to check accuracy delta.

ashley: sure. calibration prompt subset used: 

```
["In which year was the Declaration of Independence signed?", "Summarize: Recent advances in transformer quantization.", "Translate to French: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."]
```

ashley: AWQ accuracy delta vs fp16 on that set: BLEU/EM-like proxy drop ~0.6% absolute. Not huge but still within alert threshold. We need to ensure the kernel change didn't regress accuracy (unlikely but possible if there are reorderings).

perf-bot: calibration-audit for run-1756004321:\n- dataset_size: 120 prompts\n- awq_vs_fp16_exact_match_pct: 92.1 -> 91.5 (delta -0.6)\n- common_errors: small tokenization cornercases on punctuation tokens (post-quantization rounding)

ci-bot: infra test "runtime-kernel-smoke/int8-awq" failed on v2-rope-optimized with error: "kv-cache-inconsistent: mismatch layer 10". See CI job 7892.

sara: CI failure aligns with observed mismatch. Could be kernel not honoring the same kv id ordering causing cache keys to diverge.

devon: proposal: rollback selector, mark v2-rope-optimized as "experimental" behind a flag, and add a selector rule: require exact rope_scale match OR head_stride==packed_stride OR else prefer v1-generic.

ashley: +1. I'll open a PR with perf trace + reproducer and attach the calibration results. PR will include a small patch to the selector table to tighten the heuristic.

sam: I'll prepare kernel harness test vectors (qwen/mistral/mixtral/llama) and add them to CI gated on a perf-threshold. want to catch regressions earlier.

marco: FYI, for Mistral14b our head packing is different (heads=32, kv_dim=256) — that case previously gating v2 looked fine, so we should parameterize the rule by head_dim/kvdim ratio rather than only head count.

ashley: noted. timeline: I'll revert selector change today, and DEVON you'll own the follow-up heuristics. Sam/marco will add CI tests by EOW. tagging @devon @sam @marco :eyes:

devon: on it.

sam: will send WIP tests in a few hours.

ashley: thanks all, will update thread when PR is in. :rocket:
